meanings.note: Polite Jordanian title for any man ('sir / Mr') as well as 'teacher' or 'professor'.

examples.trans: Please have a seat, sir.
Good morning, gentlemen.

meanings.note: Exclamation of mild surprise or realization ('oh!').

examples.trans: Oh! My glasses are on my head!
Oh, look at the beauty of this ceiling!

meanings.note: Command to a male to wait.

examples.trans: Wait a moment, I have an idea!
The suitcase is still waiting for its owner.

meanings.note: Everyday noun for a person's or place's name; takes possessive endings directly (اسمي my name, اسمك your name).

examples.trans: What is your kind name?
My name is written here in the notebook.

meanings.note: Attached prefix ب- before nouns ('in/with'); with pronoun suffixes in Levantine it takes the stem في-: فيي ('in me'), فيك ('in/to you m.'), فيكي ('in/to you f.'), فيه ('in him/it'), فيها ('in her/it'), فينا ('in us'), فيهم ('in them').

examples.trans: Welcome to Jasmine House!
My suitcase has a red ribbon in it.

meanings.note: Everyday Levantine word (from Turkish burgu) for a metal screw.

examples.trans: I tightened the screw with the small screwdriver.
The chair needs a new screw.

meanings.note: Means 'after' (بعد المطر) and with a future span 'in' (بعد أربعين دقيقة 'in forty minutes').

examples.trans: He arrives in forty minutes.
How lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: The musical instrument.

examples.trans: The sound of the piano is warm and calm.
I learned piano when I was young.

meanings.note: Imperative ابعدوا ('step back!'); distinct from preposition بعد ('after').

examples.trans: Step back from the window, all of you!
He moved the chair slightly away from the door.

meanings.note: The number 9.

examples.trans: The quietness in the courtyard is nine out of ten!
She came back in just nine minutes!

meanings.note: The number 30.

examples.trans: They have given us thirty days in the letter.
The bill is thirty-eight dinars.

meanings.note: Used to emphasize absolute completion or exactness.

examples.trans: Its size fits you perfectly.
The street is completely empty at noon.

meanings.note: The number 2.

examples.trans: He has two left on the shelf.
Hold the torch, the two of you!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: ثابتة, plural: ثابتين).

examples.trans: Hold the torch steady on the pipe.
The flame's color is steady blue.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: جاهزة, plural: جاهزين).

examples.trans: The desk is clean and the keys are ready.
Breakfast is ready in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: جديدة, plural: جداد).

examples.trans: I am Nour, the new receptionist.
I installed a new lightbulb last week.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بجرب, بيجرب).

examples.trans: This sweater is clean and new — try it on.
We tried the new recipe and it turned out delicious.

meanings.note: The standard Levantine Arabic word for 'inside' or 'inwards'.

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
The water is flowing inside!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: جيب.

examples.trans: Put the key in the coat pocket.
The paper is in my right pocket.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: حيطان.

examples.trans: We hung the mirror on the wall.
Stone walls keep the coolness in summer.

meanings.note: Names smooth fired ceramic or porcelain, including old-style porcelain electrical fuses and glazed bowls.

examples.text: الفيوز القديم مصنوع من خزف أبيض قوي.
examples.trans: The old fuse is made of strong white porcelain.

examples.text: على الرف صحون خزف ملونة من السوق.
examples.trans: On the shelf sit colourful ceramic plates from the market.

meanings.note: In everyday Jordanian speech, خيال commonly means a cast 'shadow' or 'silhouette' as well as 'imagination'.

examples.text: شفت خيال القطة على الحيط تحت الفانوس.
examples.trans: I saw the cat's shadow on the wall beneath the lantern.

examples.text: خيال الشجرة واصل لحد باب المطبخ.
examples.trans: The tree's shadow reaches right to the kitchen door.

meanings.note: Used to describe warm weather, warm water, or a cozy feeling.

examples.trans: The bread is warm and fresh from the oven.
Sitting in the attic is cozy when it rains.

meanings.note: Essential Jordanian word used for giving directions ('go straight') or to mean doing something immediately.

examples.trans: Turn left and walk straight to the bridge.
Walk straight to the end of the street.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: دهبية, plural: دهبيين).

examples.trans: The gold tin is on the top shelf.

examples.text: فوق الباب في رسمة مفتاح دهبي.
examples.trans: Above the door there is a painted golden key.

meanings.note: With possessive suffixes (دورك 'your turn', دوري 'my turn') it marks whose turn it is next.

examples.text: هلا دورك تكبسي المفتاح يا نور!
examples.trans: Now it is your turn to press the switch, Nour!
We waited our turn in front of the pottery table.

meanings.note: Adverb formed from رسمي ('official'); used both seriously and playfully ('Room Nine officially has light!').

examples.text: الكافيه رح يفتح رسميا آخر الأسبوع.
examples.trans: The café will open officially at the end of the week.

examples.text: نور صارت رسميا موظفة الاستقبال بالنزل.
examples.trans: Nour has officially become the inn's receptionist.

ركب.gloss: to ride; take (a bus); fit cleanly

meanings.en: to ride; take (a bus); fit cleanly
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بركب, بيركب).

examples.trans: We rode the same morning bus!
The new brass thread fitted cleanly.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أسلاك.

examples.trans: The old wire needs a slight adjustment.
We checked the bell wire by the door.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: سلالم.

examples.trans: He played the musical scale slowly.
He climbed the ladder to fit the bulb.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بسمع, بيسمع).

examples.trans: Did you hear the gate bell downstairs?
Inside the courtyard we hear the tree leaves.

meanings.note: Everyday word for a year.

examples.trans: The building is eighty years old.
I have not seen him for three years.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to see, look, check' (بشوف / شاف).

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
I will see you tomorrow at breakfast.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: شبابيك.

examples.trans: The window overlooks the courtyard tree.
We painted the wooden shutters in summer.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: شغالة, plural: شغالين).

examples.trans: The light in the bathroom is working fine.
The heater is back up and running like before.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بصير, بيصير).

examples.trans: You became one of us quickly!
Did the water upstairs turn cold?

meanings.note: Everyday word confirming something is right ('right! / true!').

examples.text: صح! في صفحة تانية ورا الرسالة.
examples.trans: Right! There is a second page behind the letter.
What you say is completely true.

meanings.note: Adjective used for size (small) or age (young), masculine singular.

examples.trans: We found a little wooden train in the bag.
There are two small streets on the left.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أصوات.

examples.trans: I heard the sound of rain on the window.
His voice is calm and polite on the phone.

meanings.note: Colloquial pronunciation of the word for light.

examples.trans: The yellow light beside the bed is warm.
Turn on the light in the hallway, please.

meanings.note: Sound word for a sharp noise: a click, a pop or a crack.

examples.trans: I heard a pop from the kitchen.
Crack! The glass broke.

meanings.note: Instance noun (اسم مرة) from onomatopoeic طق ('pop, click').

examples.text: سمعنا طقة خفيفة لما فتح القفل النحاس.
examples.trans: We heard a soft click when the brass lock opened.

examples.text: اشتغلت اللمبة بهدوء بدون ولا طقة.
examples.trans: The lamp came on quietly without a single pop.

meanings.note: Collective noun for bricks or building blocks; حيط طوب is a brick wall.

examples.trans: The house is built of brick and stone.
They brought new bricks for the wall.

meanings.note: Everyday Levantine noun for darkness (related to معتم 'dark, unlit').

examples.text: شغل الفانوس عشان ما نمشي بالعتمة.
examples.trans: Turn on the lantern so we do not walk in the dark.

examples.text: راحت العتمة أول ما ضوت لمبة السقف.
examples.trans: The darkness vanished as soon as the ceiling lamp lit up.

meanings.note: Can refer to a cardboard box, a tin can, or a small container.

examples.trans: The gold tin is on the top shelf.
I saved this old wooden box.

meanings.note: Standard preposition for 'on', 'upon', or 'to'.

examples.trans: Your glasses are on your forehead!
Say hello to Salma for me!

meanings.note: Means 'about' (عن الزبدة), 'off / away from' (عن جبيني), and appears in عن جد ('really!') and عن إذنك ('excuse me').

examples.trans: I will carry the suitcase up for you.
I heard your voices about the butter!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for a room in a house or building.

examples.trans: We have eight comfortable rooms at the guesthouse.
Room four is ready and clean.

meanings.note: Refers to a lid, cover, or sometimes a blanket.

examples.trans: Put the lid on the pot.
In winter I sleep under a heavy blanket.

فرش.gloss: to spread; lay out (cloth or light)

meanings.en: to spread; lay out (cloth or light)
meanings.note: Used literally for spreading a tablecloth or rug and figuratively for warm light spreading across a room.

examples.text: فرشت سلمى شراشف بيضا عالطاولات الخشب.
examples.trans: Salma spread white cloths over the wooden tables.

examples.text: ضو الصبح بيفرش دفا حلو عالساحة.
examples.trans: Morning light spreads lovely warmth across the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أفران.

examples.text: لفائف القرفة طلعت من الفرن هلا.
examples.trans: The cinnamon rolls just came out of the oven.
The bakery down the street bakes in the morning.

meanings.note: Loanword from English 'fuse'; when one blows, people say الفيوز ضرب.

examples.trans: I changed the fuse and the light came back.
The fuse box is next to the door.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: قديمة, plural: قدام).

examples.trans: The courtyard has an old jasmine tree.
The old hardware shop is past the bridge.

meanings.note: Refers to the material glass, a pane of glass, or sometimes a glass bottle.

examples.trans: Look at the courtyard through the window glass.
We wiped the glass this morning until it shone.

meanings.note: Any fabric; سلك قماش is old cloth-covered electrical wire.

examples.trans: She bought blue fabric for the curtains.
This fabric is very soft.

meanings.note: The Amman verb for pressing a button, doorbell or switch.

examples.text: اكبس الزر الأحمر عشان يفتح الباب.
examples.trans: Press the red button to open the door.

examples.text: كبست الجرس مرتين وما حدا فتح.
examples.trans: I pressed the bell twice and nobody opened.

كبسة.gloss: a press; a click (of a button)

meanings.en: a press; a click (of a button)
meanings.note: One press of a button: بكبسة وحدة 'with one click'.

examples.trans: With one press the machine starts.
Two presses on the bell means it is me.

meanings.note: A highly versatile quantifier used to mean 'all of', 'every', or 'the whole'.

examples.trans: Tell me everything I need to know.
Everyone is happy in the courtyard today.

meanings.note: Indispensable Levantine and Egyptian particle meaning 'also', 'too', or 'as well'.

examples.text: التفكير السريع أنقذ الفطور كمان مرة!
examples.trans: Quick thinking saved breakfast once again!
And I missed you too.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for 'no' or 'not', used exactly like Standard Arabic.

examples.trans: No, lift the handle first.
Do not worry, ma'am.

meanings.note: Used to mark the limit of a time period, distance, or extent in colloquial Jordanian.

examples.trans: We waited until you called us.
I stayed up until midnight.

meanings.note: Very common Jordanian word to indicate that an action is ongoing or hasn't happened yet.

examples.trans: Is your cup still intact?
Nobody has written anything yet.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: لوحات.

examples.text: شوف لوحة المفاتيح الخشب ورا المكتب.
examples.trans: Look at the wooden key board behind the desk.
We wiped the dust off the brass plate.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مستحيلة, plural: —).

examples.trans: There is no way I would bother a guest with our problems!
It is impossible for us to forget this week.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: مطابخ.

examples.trans: The smell of bread is coming from the kitchen.
The guesthouse kitchen is spacious and clean.

meanings.note: Levantine adjective describing frosted lamp glass (قزاز مغبش) or fogged-up spectacles.

examples.text: القزاز المغبش بيخلي ضو اللمبة هادي للعين.
examples.trans: Frosted glass makes the lamp light gentle on the eyes.

examples.text: نظارتي مغبشة من بخار إبريق الشاي!
examples.trans: My glasses are fogged up from the steam of the teapot!

meanings.note: Means both a door key and a mechanic's spanner/wrench (مفتاح حديد iron wrench).

examples.trans: Here is the key to room four.
We have eight brass keys on the board.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مفتوحة, plural: مفتوحين).

examples.trans: Is the hardware shop open right now?
Here is to neighbours and our open gates!

meanings.note: One of the most basic Arabic prepositions indicating origin.

examples.trans: I am Salma from the kitchen.
Breakfast is from seven-thirty to ten.

meanings.note: Passive participle of وصل ('to connect, join').

examples.text: السلك النحاس موصول منيح بعلبة الكهربا.
examples.trans: The copper wire is firmly connected to the electrical box.
The sunroom is connected to the back hallway.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بنادي, بينادي).

examples.trans: Do we call each other by first name here?
Salma called everyone to breakfast.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: ناعمة, plural: ناعمين); سكر ناعم means 'powdered sugar'.

examples.trans: I brought two soft pillows for the attic.
Lemon cake dusted with powdered sugar.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بناول, بيناول).

examples.trans: Hand me the heavy iron wrench.
Pass me the teacup, please.

meanings.note: Vivid Levantine word for a tiny pinch or scrap; ولا نتفة means 'not a single scrap / zero'.

examples.text: ما ضل ولا نتفة غبرة عالرفوف.
examples.trans: Not a single speck of dust is left on the shelves.

examples.text: حطي نتفة قرفة صغيرة فوق الكيك.
examples.trans: Put a tiny pinch of cinnamon on top of the cake.

meanings.note: Used for the metal or objects made of it.

examples.trans: We polished the brass keys in the morning.
The brass pot is old and engraved.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for clean or tidy.

examples.trans: The desk is clean and the room is ready.

examples.text: آسف نقطت مي على أرضكم النظيفة.
examples.trans: Sorry I dripped water onto your clean floor.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بنزل, بينزل).

examples.trans: The guests will come down at half past seven.
I came down to ask about the sink water.

meanings.note: Cardinal number or used as an indefinite pronoun.

examples.trans: Not a single scratch on the cup!
The gate rang with one strong ring.

meanings.note: Vocative particle used when addressing someone directly.

examples.trans: Good morning, Tariq!
Oh, how lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: Very common interjection used to urge action or to say goodbye ('yalla bye').

examples.trans: Come on, let us bring the bag down into the light!
Let us go check out the room right now!
